How This Forecast Works

This report predicts cycle volume for the next 90 days in the New York market.

The model uses a daily snapshot table. Each row is one cycle at one point in time. The model learns how likely a cycle is to complete or cancel, based on current stage and patient factors.

The forecast has three parts:

  1. Active cycles in the pipeline
  2. New starts expected from current NPV flow
  3. Return cycles from prior patients

The model runs backtests on recent cutoffs. Backtests compare forecast values to true observed values. This gives error metrics and interval bands.

Use this report to answer two questions:

  1. How much work volume is expected by day and by month
  2. Where the volume comes from, and how stable the model is over time

Covariates used in the model

The forecast is built from a cause-specific survival model that uses the following patient and cycle features to predict completion and cancellation risk:

  • patient_age_c: patient age, centered so the model compares the effect of age relative to a typical case.
  • patient_insurance_status: coverage type, whether Kindbody employer benefit, self-pay, or other insurance.
  • attempt_type: KindEMR cycle type (e.g. egg freezing, IVF, FET, oocyte thaw).
  • first_attempt: whether this is the patient’s first treatment attempt.
  • prior_cancel_cat: prior cancellation history, grouped into a small set of categories to capture repeat-cycle risk.
  • current_stage: the patient’s current treatment stage in the cycle (e.g. new patient visit, cycle plan entered, cycle started)
  • log_days_in_stage: the log of how long the patient has been in the current stage.
  • log_monthly_npvs: the log of monthly new patient volume, which helps capture demand and referral momentum.
  • season_[sin/cos 1-2]: cyclic terms to capture seasonality (2 sine and 2 cosine transformations of the month).
